wide/recall: An autoencoder squeezes its input through a narrow middle, then rebuilds it.
wide/flip: A sparse autoencoder turns that around. If a model stores more features than it has dimensions, the middle must be wider: often eight or sixteen times d.
wide/dict: Each middle unit is a feature, and each has its own direction in the decoder. Together they form a dictionary.
loss/err: Training balances two terms. The reconstruction error asks the rebuild to match x.
loss/l1: The L1 penalty adds lambda times the sum of the features, which the ReLU keeps from going negative. For the code zero, two, zero, zero, a half, zero, zero, zero, with lambda at zero point one, the penalty is zero point two five.
loss/zero: Every active feature costs something, so small, unhelpful ones are pushed all the way to zero. Only a few stay on for any one input.
rebuild/sum: The rebuild is the sum of each active feature times its direction. Here, two times feature one's direction, one, zero, plus a half times feature four's, zero, two. That is two, one.
rebuild/meaning: Because each input uses only a few features, each feature tends to stand for one thing. That is what sparsity buys: a readable dictionary of what the model represents.
